utah.temperature: Under transient ridging and positive 500-hPa height anomalies and consistent with the consolidation of reforecast calibrated GEFS and ECMWF temperatures, enhanced probabilities for above normal temperatures are predicted across the southwestern CONUS and most of the eastern CONUS, excluding northern New England where tools are less consistent.
utah.precipitation: Ahead of a predicted trough and with enhanced moisture flow from the tropical Pacific, probabilities for above normal precipitation are enhanced for the Southwest, the Four Corners region, and southern and central Rockies.

ne.temperature: Under transient ridging and positive 500-hPa height anomalies and consistent with the consolidation of reforecast calibrated GEFS and ECMWF temperatures, enhanced probabilities for above normal temperatures are predicted across the southwestern CONUS and most of the eastern CONUS, excluding northern New England where tools are less consistent.
ne.precipitation: Above normal precipitation is favored across the central and eastern CONUS, consistent with reforecast calibrated precipitation forecasts from the ECMWF and GEFS ensembles.

utah.temperature: Above normal temperatures are likely for most of the western CONUS, as a ridge and positive 500-hPa height anomalies amplify over the region during the period.
utah.precipitation: Under a predicted ridge, below normal precipitation is favored over most of the northwestern CONUS, from most of the West Coast, excluding Southern California, northeastward across the northern Rockies into the northern High Plains.

ne.temperature: Near normal temperatures are favored for much of the northern central and northeastern CONUS, where temperature tools are inconsistent or show weak signals.
ne.precipitation: Under a predicted ridge, below normal precipitation is favored over most of the northwestern CONUS, from most of the West Coast, excluding Southern California, northeastward across the northern Rockies into the northern High Plains.

ne.temperature: Similarly, some models also indicate weak chances for below-normal temperatures over the East, but there was not enough evidence or support for a tilt toward below-normal temperatures in the Outlook.
ne.precipitation: A broad swath of elevated below-normal precipitation chances are indicated from the Northern Plains to the Northeast, dipping into the Lower Mississippi and Tennessee Valleys.
